runs.text: Pattani Malay are descendants of Malay Muslims who embraced Islam since the 14th century. Their Islamic faith has given the Pattani a distinct identity in Buddhist Thailand. They are a very tight community and take a lot of pride in being Malay.

Most Patani Malay people live in the three southernmost provinces of Thailand: Pattani, Yala, and Narathiwat. They make up over 80% of the population of these provinces. They are also found in parts of Songkhla Province. Some Patani Malay live around Bangkok. Narathiwat is one of the poorest provinces in Thailand.
Many Pattani Malay live in rural villages and make their living by fishing, painting boats called kolae, tapping rubber, and growing fruit and vegetables. The Pattani Malay have faced government
oppression
because of ongoing unrest and armed conflict linked to the Pattani Malay National Revolutionary Front (BRN).

In the early 19th century, a strong missionary movement from the West began throughout Thailand. Missionaries made significant contributions to Thai border communities in the fields of medicine, education, and religion. In 1953, a missionary entered Yala Province and began the ministry. In the 1960s and 1970s, more missionaries entered the Pattani area for mission work. Despite the continuous missionary efforts, why do the Pattani people remain FPGs?
The Pattani people, who have lived in Thailand for generations, are still called ‘Kunak’, which means guest. We pray that the Pattani Malay will soon be
free from oppression
and become citizens of God’s Kingdom, not just guests in their own country.
“The LORD is
a stronghold for the oppressed
, a stronghold in times of trouble. And those who know your name put their trust in you, for you, O LORD, have not forsaken those who seek you.
Psalm 9:9-10 (ESV)
Pray that the Pattani Malay will know that God is a
stronghold for the oppressed
and a healer for the hurting.
Pray that the Holy Spirit will open hearts and eyes to see that God cares deeply for the oppressed.
Pray for a renewed mission movement among local, global churches, and mission organizations to reach the Pattani Malay.
Pray for God’s peace in the Pattani region and for people to find the source of life in Jesus.
Some Christians are helping with relief work after severe flooding in 2025. Pray that this ministry will impact the Pattani Malay both now and into the future.
